page.title: The tinyactors command
page.description: The tinyactors command compiles, checks, draws, compares and runs charts, and reads the snapshots and blobs a host writes.

hero.headline: Check, compare and run charts from a shell
hero.lede: tinyactors finds the path to a state, the change that breaks running actors, and every actor in a snapshot. Each answer comes as Markdown, JSON or XML.

section.heading: One program per platform, checked by mise
section.p: Each release of tinyactors-core carries the command for Linux and macOS, on x86_64 and arm64. mise picks your machine's archive, checks it against the release's checksums and puts tinyactors on your path.

claim.statement: One Linux binary runs on every distribution
claim.p: The Linux program is linked statically against musl, so one file serves glibc and musl systems alike. The macOS one loads only libSystem.

claim.statement: The command runs charts on quickjs
claim.p: It carries the host and the ECMAScript datamodel, so tinyactors run runs your charts with no language package installed.

section.heading: Each command answers one question
section.p: Each page below is made from the command's own help, with its examples run on an order and a payment chart.

section.heading: Programs read the same answer as JSON
section.p: With -f json or -f xml, every command answers with the members its Markdown shows, in the same order. A CI job reads charts[0].states from JSON.

claim.statement: Exit statuses are part of the answer
claim.p: diff --exit-code exits with 1 on a difference, lint --deny on a finding, and fmt --check on a file to rewrite.

section.heading: Drive a host, read what it wrote

term.link: Drive a host from a script

item.text: A script spawns actors, answers their sends and moves the clock over JSON-RPC.
A snapshot file holds every actor of a host, and the command reads it without restoring it.
